metadata.note: General educational guidance. Confirm diagnosis and follow local agricultural recommendations before treatment.

diseases.name: bacterial_leaf_blight
symptoms: Yellowing along leaf margins
Leaf drying that may progress from the tip
Wilting or drying of affected leaves
prevention: Use healthy seed and locally recommended resistant varieties
Maintain balanced fertilizer application
Inspect crops regularly and manage infected residues appropriately
treatment: Confirm the diagnosis with a local agricultural expert
Follow locally approved management recommendations
Avoid applying pesticides without confirming suitability for the crop and disease

diseases.name: blast
symptoms: Spindle-shaped leaf lesions
Lesions with pale centers and darker margins
In severe cases, damage to neck or panicle tissues
prevention: Use recommended resistant varieties where available
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer
Monitor fields for symptoms and follow recommended crop management practices
treatment: Confirm disease identity and severity
Seek local agricultural advice on approved fungicides when necessary
Follow the product label and local regulations

diseases.name: brown_spot
symptoms: Brown oval or circular spots on leaves
Spots that may develop yellow margins
Reduced plant vigor in severe cases
prevention: Maintain balanced crop nutrition
Use healthy seed
Improve field management and investigate possible nutrient deficiencies
treatment: Confirm the cause of the symptoms
Address verified nutrient or crop-management problems
Use approved plant-protection products only when recommended

diseases.name: Early Blight
symptoms: Brown leaf spots that may develop concentric rings
Yellowing around affected tissue
Older leaves may be affected first
prevention: Rotate crops with suitable non-host crops
Reduce prolonged leaf wetness where practical
Remove or manage infected crop residues
treatment: Confirm the disease before treatment
Use locally approved fungicides only when appropriate
Follow label directions and resistance-management advice

diseases.name: Late Blight
symptoms: Water-soaked-looking leaf patches
Rapidly expanding dark lesions in favorable conditions
Possible white growth near lesion margins in humid weather
prevention: Monitor local late-blight warnings
Use healthy seed tubers and recommended varieties
Avoid unnecessary prolonged leaf wetness
treatment: Seek prompt local agricultural advice because the disease can spread rapidly
Use only approved products appropriate for late blight
Follow all label instructions and pre-harvest intervals

diseases.name: Tomato___Bacterial_spot
symptoms: Small dark lesions on leaves
Possible yellow halos around lesions
Possible spots on stems or fruit
prevention: Use healthy seed and transplants
Avoid handling plants while foliage is wet
Sanitize tools and manage infected plant debris
treatment: Confirm the bacterial diagnosis
Remove severely affected material where appropriate
Consult local agricultural guidance about approved management options

diseases.name: Tomato___Early_blight
symptoms: Dark leaf lesions that may have concentric rings
Yellowing around lesions
Symptoms often begin on older leaves
prevention: Rotate crops where possible
Avoid overhead irrigation when practical
Manage infected plant debris
treatment: Confirm the disease
Improve watering and crop hygiene practices
Use approved fungicides only when locally recommended

diseases.name: Tomato___Late_blight
symptoms: Water-soaked-looking leaf lesions
Dark, rapidly spreading lesions in favorable weather
Possible white growth near lesion margins in humid conditions
prevention: Monitor crops and local disease alerts
Avoid prolonged leaf wetness where practical
Use healthy planting material
treatment: Seek prompt expert guidance if late blight is suspected
Use only locally approved products appropriate for the confirmed disease
Follow label directions and pre-harvest intervals

diseases.name: Downy_Mildew
symptoms: Yellowish or oily-looking spots on the upper leaf surface
Possible white growth beneath leaves in humid conditions
Affected leaves may brown and dry
prevention: Improve airflow through appropriate canopy management
Monitor weather and inspect leaves regularly
Avoid irrigation practices that unnecessarily wet foliage
treatment: Confirm the disease with a local grape-production expert
Use only locally approved products appropriate for downy mildew
Follow label directions and resistance-management recommendations

diseases.name: Powdery_Mildew
symptoms: White or gray powder-like growth on leaves
Distorted or stunted young growth in some cases
Affected berries may develop surface damage
prevention: Maintain suitable canopy airflow
Inspect new growth regularly
Use locally recommended resistant varieties when practical
treatment: Confirm the diagnosis
Consult local grape-production guidance for suitable approved treatments
Follow product labels and resistance-management advice
